items.question: What services does Mauritania Concierge provide?
items.answer: Mauritania Concierge runs three fully active service lines with the same attention and dedication: tourist expeditions across Mauritania (Adrar, the iron ore train, the Richat Structure, the Banc d’Arguin…), business delegation services in Nouakchott and nationwide, and intercity transport between all cities of Mauritania. We also arrange anything else on request.

items.question: Do you provide intercity transport in Mauritania?
items.answer: Yes. We drive travelers and business teams between all cities of Mauritania: Nouakchott, Nouadhibou, Atar, Rosso, Kiffa, Kaédi, Néma, Zouérat and more, door to door, one way or return, with a sedan, a 4x4 or a minibus and a professional driver.

items.question: Can you arrange something that is not listed on the website?
items.answer: Yes. Tell us what you need and we arrange it: vehicle rental with driver, apartment or villa rental, interpreters, local guides, SIM cards, meeting rooms, appointments, event logistics or a last-minute change. Contact us on WhatsApp or by email.

items.question: Do you organize tourist expeditions in Mauritania?
items.answer: Yes. We organize six signature expeditions: the Adrar and its ancient cities, the iron ore train, the Richat Structure, the Banc d’Arguin National Park, the culture of Nouakchott and Nouadhibou, and Diawling National Park with the Senegal River, with vehicles, drivers and guides.

items.question: Is Mauritania safe for foreigners and investors?
items.answer: Yes, Mauritania is safe, especially for business travelers and tourists. The capital Nouakchott is very secure. However, having a local concierge and private driver significantly enhances your comfort, security, and ease of navigation.

items.question: Do you provide airport pickup at Nouakchott International Airport?
items.answer: Absolutely. Our VIP airport pickup service includes a meet & greet, help with luggage, and a private air-conditioned vehicle waiting to transfer you to your hotel.

items.question: Can you help business travelers and delegations?
items.answer: Yes, we specialize in assisting NGOs, diplomats, and investors. We coordinate your transportation, manage schedules, and provide translation services for smooth business operations.

items.question: Do you speak English?
items.answer: Yes, our team provides full assistance and translation services in English, French, and Arabic.

Destinations.title: Where the Desert Whispers Its Oldest Stories
Destinations.subtitle: Follow the ancient caravan roads to cities of stone and starlight. Ride through the night on a train of iron across the Sahara, watch a giant eye open in the heart of the desert, see a million wings rise above the Atlantic, share three glasses of tea on a golden shore, and drift along the river where Mauritania turns green. Six journeys, one land that never leaves you.

Destinations.homeSubtitle: Six signature expeditions, from the desert to the Atlantic and the river.

adrar.name: Adrar & the Ancient Cities
adrar.tagline: Caravan cities, manuscripts and endless dunes
adrar.short: Chinguetti, Ouadane, the Terjit oasis and the great dunes: the heart of Saharan Mauritania.
adrar.intro: The Adrar is the soul of the Mauritanian Sahara. For centuries, caravans crossed its plateaus to reach the ksour, fortified trading cities where scholars copied manuscripts that are still kept in family libraries today. Chinguetti, Ouadane, Tichitt and Oualata form a UNESCO World Heritage site, surrounded by golden ergs, black cliffs and hidden oases.

highlights.title: UNESCO Ancient Cities
highlights.desc: Walk the stone alleys of Chinguetti and Ouadane, among the great historic cities of the Sahara.

highlights.title: Centuries-Old Manuscripts
highlights.desc: Visit the family libraries of Chinguetti that preserve Qurans and scientific texts.

highlights.title: Oases & Dunes
highlights.desc: Swim in the spring of Terjit, sleep under the stars and watch sunset over the Amatlich dunes.

sites.name: Chinguetti
sites.desc: The seventh holy city of Islam for many, with its historic mosque and libraries.

sites.name: Ouadane
sites.desc: A spectacular stone city built on a cliff, gateway to the Richat Structure.

sites.name: Terjit
sites.desc: A palm-shaded spring at the bottom of a gorge, a true oasis.

sites.name: Atar
sites.desc: The capital of the Adrar and starting point of every expedition.

sites.name: Tichitt & Oualata
sites.desc: Remote ksour famous for their decorated architecture, on request.

adrar.access: About 450 km from Nouakchott to Atar by road, then 4x4 tracks.

richat-structure.name: Richat Structure, the Eye of the Sahara
richat-structure.tagline: A 40 km circle visible from space
richat-structure.short: A giant geological formation so large that astronauts use it as a landmark from orbit.
richat-structure.intro: In the middle of the Sahara, near Ouadane, concentric rings of rock form a circle about 40 km wide: the Guelb er Richat, known as the Eye of the Sahara or the Eye of Africa. Long thought to be a meteorite crater, it is in fact an ancient eroded dome. Seen from space it is breathtaking; on the ground, crossing its rings by 4x4 is an unforgettable adventure.

highlights.title: Visible From Space
highlights.desc: One of the most famous landmarks on Earth for astronauts aboard the International Space Station.

highlights.title: 4x4 Expedition
highlights.desc: Cross the rings with experienced desert drivers and reach the heart of the structure.

highlights.title: A Night in the Desert
highlights.desc: Camp under one of the clearest night skies in the world.

sites.name: The outer rings
sites.desc: Ridges of quartzite that draw the famous circles seen from above.

sites.name: The central zone
sites.desc: The heart of the eye, a vast plain of rocks and sand.

sites.name: Ouadane
sites.desc: The ancient city nearby, perfect to combine with the Adrar expedition.

richat-structure.access: Via Atar and Ouadane, then about 40 km of off-road tracks.

banc-d-arguin.name: Banc d'Arguin National Park
banc-d-arguin.tagline: Wildlife and the wild Atlantic coast
banc-d-arguin.short: Where the Sahara meets the ocean: a UNESCO park and one of the world’s great bird sanctuaries.
banc-d-arguin.intro: Between Nouakchott and Nouadhibou, the desert dunes run straight into the Atlantic. The Banc d'Arguin National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage site, protects shallow waters and islands where more than two million migratory birds spend the winter. Here the Imraguen fishermen still sail traditional lanches, as motor boats are not allowed in the park.

highlights.title: Bird Paradise
highlights.desc: Flamingos, pelicans, spoonbills and huge flocks of migratory shorebirds.

highlights.title: Desert Meets Ocean
highlights.desc: Golden dunes falling into turquoise water, a landscape found almost nowhere else.

highlights.title: Imraguen Culture
highlights.desc: Meet the fishing communities and sail on their traditional boats.

sites.name: Iwik & the islands
sites.desc: Boat trips around the islands where the birds gather.

sites.name: Cap Tafarit
sites.desc: Wild beaches and cliffs on the edge of the desert.

sites.name: Imraguen villages
sites.desc: Traditional fishing life along the coast.

banc-d-arguin.access: About 250 km north of Nouakchott on the Nouadhibou road, then desert tracks.

nouakchott-nouadhibou.name: Culture & Urban Experiences
nouakchott-nouadhibou.tagline: Nouakchott and Nouadhibou: an introduction to Mauritanian culture
nouakchott-nouadhibou.short: Fish markets, tea ceremonies, crafts and the famous iron ore train: Mauritania as it lives today.
nouakchott-nouadhibou.intro: The best introduction to Mauritania starts in its cities. In Nouakchott, hundreds of painted pirogues return to the beach every afternoon, the markets are full of colour and every visit begins with three glasses of tea. In Nouadhibou, on the Atlantic, you can watch one of the longest trains in the world arrive from the desert, and explore Cap Blanc and its coast.

highlights.title: Fishermen’s Beach
highlights.desc: The most vivid scene in Nouakchott: pirogues, nets and the daily catch at sunset.

highlights.title: The Tea Ceremony
highlights.desc: Share the famous three glasses of tea and Mauritanian hospitality.

highlights.title: The Iron Ore Train
highlights.desc: In Nouadhibou, see a train up to 2.5 km long arrive from the Sahara.

sites.name: Nouakchott fish market
sites.desc: Pirogues, fishermen and traders on the Atlantic beach.

sites.name: Markets & crafts
sites.desc: Silver jewellery, leatherwork, fabrics and spices.

sites.name: Nouadhibou & Cap Blanc
sites.desc: The fishing port, the coast and the Cap Blanc reserve.

sites.name: Mauritanian cuisine
sites.desc: Thieboudienne, grilled fish, méchoui and local specialities.

nouakchott-nouadhibou.bestSeason: All year (most pleasant October to May)
nouakchott-nouadhibou.access: Nouakchott is your arrival point; Nouadhibou is about 470 km north by road or a short flight.

diawling-senegal-river.name: Diawling National Park & the Senegal River
diawling-senegal-river.short: Wetlands, birdlife and river villages along the Senegal River, a completely different Mauritania.
diawling-senegal-river.intro: In the south, the desert gives way to the green valley of the Senegal River. Diawling National Park protects the wetlands of the lower delta, a refuge for pelicans, flamingos and herons, and part of a cross-border biosphere reserve with Senegal. Along the river, Haalpulaar, Soninké and Wolof villages, pirogues and rice fields reveal the African side of Mauritania.

highlights.title: Wetlands & Birdlife
highlights.desc: Pelicans, flamingos, herons and many more in the basins of the Diawling.

highlights.title: Life on the River
highlights.desc: Pirogues, fishermen and river markets along the Senegal River.

highlights.title: Cultural Diversity
highlights.desc: Discover the Haalpulaar, Soninké and Wolof communities of the valley.

sites.name: Diawling National Park
sites.desc: Lagoons, basins and dunes of the lower Senegal delta.

sites.name: Rosso
sites.desc: The river town on the border with Senegal.

sites.name: Kaédi & the valley
sites.desc: River ports, villages and farmland further upstream.

diawling-senegal-river.access: About 200 km south of Nouakchott to Rosso, then tracks into the park.

iron-ore-train.name: The Iron Ore Train
iron-ore-train.tagline: A night aboard one of the longest trains in the world
iron-ore-train.short: Ride the legendary Sahara train between Zouérat and Nouadhibou: up to 2.5 km of wagons, around 700 km of desert and a sky full of stars.
iron-ore-train.intro: Every day, one of the longest and heaviest trains on Earth leaves the iron mines of Zouérat and crosses the Sahara to the port of Nouadhibou: around 700 km of desert and up to 2.5 km of wagons. For travelers it is a legend: climbing onto an ore wagon at Choum, watching the dunes roll by, sharing tea with fellow passengers and falling asleep under the stars. We turn this raw adventure into a safe, well-organized experience.

highlights.title: A Legendary Ride
highlights.desc: One of the longest trains in the world, a journey travelers talk about for the rest of their lives.

highlights.title: The Sahara by Night
highlights.desc: Sunset over the dunes, a sky full of stars and sunrise from the top of a wagon.

highlights.title: Prepared & Accompanied
highlights.desc: An experienced guide, water and meals, blankets for the night and transfers at both ends.

sites.name: Choum
sites.desc: The desert station where travelers coming from the Adrar board the train.

sites.name: The open Sahara
sites.desc: Hours of dunes, stony plains and plateaus with no road in sight.

sites.name: Nouadhibou
sites.desc: Arrival on the Atlantic coast, gateway to Cap Blanc and the Banc d’Arguin.

sites.name: Zouérat
sites.desc: The mining town where the train begins its journey, on request.

iron-ore-train.bestSeason: November to March (cold nights: bring warm clothes)
iron-ore-train.access: Board at Choum, about 2 hours from Atar, or at Nouadhibou for the journey inland.
